| **Measures** | **RNA** |

## My reading

I had a look again at the papers I have. Miao and the others from this year is probably the
best paper we have on **transcriptomes of blood brain barrier capillary endothelial cells**, and
on how they did the analysis. But for us specifically, if we want to concentrate on endothelial
cells, apparently there is **no identical pipeline** we could use.

There is something by Brendo which **identifies genes selectively enriched in brain
microvascular endothelial cells versus endothelial cells from other tissues**, using **bulk RNA
sequencing**. The important thing here is that it shows how it works with **multiple datasets
and quality control**.

Now I am a bit confused as to how to approach this currently, assuming we want to use
endothelial cells. Miao et al. showed that even if they looked at a very broad gene selection,
in a brain part I do not remember, there was only a small part which overlapped in gene
expression between the species, and most of them were **transporter proteins**.

There is one graph that I want to understand in order to figure out how we want to continue.

## Checks against the paper

- **Is there a pipeline identical to this project?** Not here. Brendo compares brain
  endothelium against other tissues' endothelium within human only, which matches this
  project's enrichment step rather than its cross-species step.
- **Which brain part did Miao look at, and how much overlapped?** Mouse was whole brain
  vasculature; human was post-mortem brain and tissue next to gliomas. The overlap was broad
  (correlation 0.68). The genes that differed between species, 169 and 386, were where the
  SLC transporters stood out.
